mascot: Penny the Penguin — a neat little penguin who lines up words like snowballs to build perfect sentences.

slides.title: What Is a Sentence? 💭
slides.text: A sentence is a group of words that tells a complete thought! 'The dog is big' is a sentence — we understand it fully!
slides.spoken: A sentence tells a complete thought, like 'The dog is big!'

slides.title: Start with a Capital 👆
slides.text: Every sentence starts with a CAPITAL letter. "The cat runs." — see that big T at the start?
slides.spoken: Every sentence starts with a capital letter!

slides.title: End with a Mark 🔚
slides.text: Every sentence needs an ending mark! A full stop (.) for telling, a question mark (?) for asking, an exclamation mark (!) for wow!
slides.spoken: Sentences end with a mark: a dot, a question mark or an exclamation!

slides.title: Words in Order 🧩
slides.text: Words must be in the right order: 'I like mangoes' makes sense. 'Mangoes like I' is silly! Order matters!
slides.spoken: Words go in the right order: I like mangoes — not mangoes like I!

slides.title: Telling or Asking? 🤔
slides.text: A telling sentence tells us something: 'The sun is hot.' An asking sentence asks: 'Where is my ball?' Can you tell them apart?
slides.spoken: Telling sentences tell. Asking sentences ask. Can you tell them apart?

challenges.question: Every sentence starts with a ___
challenges.hint: Look at any book — what is the very first letter of a sentence?
challenges.misconception: Every sentence starts with a CAPITAL letter!

challenges.question: A telling sentence ends with a ___
challenges.hint: When we tell something and stop, what little mark ends the line?
challenges.misconception: A telling sentence ends with a full stop (.) — like 'The sun is hot.'

challenges.question: Which sentence is written correctly?
challenges.hint: It needs a capital at the start AND a full stop at the end!
challenges.misconception: 'The dog is big.' is correct: capital T at the start and a full stop at the end!

challenges.question: Drag the words to build the sentence: 'I like mangoes.'
challenges.hint: First comes I, then like, then mangoes!
challenges.misconception: The sentence is 'I like mangoes.' — I first, like second, mangoes last!

challenges.question: Which sentence asks something?
challenges.hint: One of these sentences wants an answer back!
challenges.misconception: 'Where is my ball?' asks something — it needs an answer!

challenges.question: A sentence that asks something ends with a ___
challenges.hint: When we ask a question, which mark goes at the end?
challenges.misconception: An asking sentence ends with a question mark (?) — 'Where is my ball?'

challenges.question: Which one is a complete sentence?
challenges.hint: A complete sentence tells a whole thought: who and what they do!
challenges.misconception: 'The cat sleeps.' is complete — we know who (the cat) and what (sleeps). 'In the box' and 'big and brown' are only fragments!

challenges.question: Drag each one! Is it a real sentence or not?
challenges.hint: 'The sun is hot.' and 'I love my school.' are full thoughts. 'Under the tree' and 'is jumping' are not!
challenges.misconception: A sentence needs a complete thought. 'The sun is hot.' and 'I love my school.' are sentences; 'under the tree' and 'is jumping' are not!
